lens: Calm/Headspace confidence: reduce call anxiety, warm palette, guided warm-ups before calls
name: Warm Rehearsal
one_liner: A calm practice room for hard calls: breathe, rehearse with a persona, get one whispered cue at a time, then reflect on evidence from your own words.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the Calm/Headspace lens: warm paper-and-terracotta palette, a breathing presence ring instead of the blurry orb, a 60-second warm-up before every call, and a pre-call confidence check compared against the post-call result. One change: calm must not mean soft. Research showed Second Nature, Hyperbound and Yoodli all sell realism and live coaching, so the palette is the differentiator and a Hot persona tier stays adversarial. Best Mobbin matches: Fireflies' live-assist panel and Visitors' score ring. Self-estimates for the council to verify: A 7, B 7, C 7, D 6, E 6, F1 5, F2 6, F3 3 (3 = leaning worth building).

palette.use: Primary CTA and active states (about 5.1:1 with white)
Whispered coach cue accent; cue card background uses honey-soft #FCF0D6
Dark Dusk mode page background for night practice

design_language.typography: Fraunces 600 with optical sizing for titles and grade letters; Inter 400/500/600 for UI and transcript; tabular-nums on every score. Scale 40/32/24/18/16/14, body 16px minimum on mobile.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 20px card radius, 999px pill buttons, 1px warm line borders. Depth comes from tinted fills, not heavy shadows. The presence ring is the only glow, kept at low opacity.
design_language.motion: Breathing rhythm: a 6-second inhale and exhale ring during warm-up and while the persona speaks (scale tied to audio level). Cue cards ease in over 240ms and fade after 8s. prefers-reduced-motion swaps rings for static states and cross-fades.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.75px stroke with rounded caps. No emoji. One icon per action label; mic and breath icons mark voice and warm-up.
design_language.theme_modes: Paper (light) is the default. Dusk (dark) follows prefers-color-scheme and has a manual toggle. Tokens are defined on :root and redefined for dark, so night practice keeps the same calm rhythm.

navigation_and_ia: Desktop: 72px icon rail (Practice, Library, Progress, Team, Settings) plus a cmd+K command palette for personas. Mobile: bottom tab bar with the same four. The live call switches to full focus mode and hides chrome. Routes: /, /library, /library/new, /practice/[id], /call/[id], /debrief/[id], /progress, /team. The scenario dropdown is replaced by the library, so pre-call always shows one chosen persona. The glass header is removed.

screens.layout: Four steps on a slim top rail: Source, Persona, Scenario, Rehearse. Step 1 shows entry cards for a job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP text or a pasted call. screens.layout: Calm arrival page. Center: persona portrait and name, 'What they care about' (two bullets), your goal (one line), and the talk track as six soft steps, collapsed by default. Right: a 60-second warm-up ring (6s inhale, 6s exhale) with an optional record-your-opening-line step. Below: confidence check (1 to 5), Voice/Text toggle with mic test, coaching setting (Whisper, Quiet, Off), and a primary Begin when ready button.

screens.layout: Three zones. Center: presence ring with persona name and Speaking or Listening label, transcript in calm bubbles with soft turn dividers, composer and mute. Right rail (320px): a coach card with one whispered cue at a time (14 words or fewer, honey background, Why? expander, fades after 8s), plum objection alerts, a six-step talk-track ribbon that checks off as steps are covered, and a Live read of five criteria as thin bars with trend arrows. Top right: timer, Pause and breathe (no score penalty), Wrap up. Red stays reserved for hang-up.
screens.key_components: Presence ring, transcript, whisper cue card, objection alert, talk-track ribbon, live-read bars, numbers toggle (off by default), Pause and breathe, Wrap up.
screens.change_vs_today: A chat app with no coaching becomes a coached call: real-time cues, talk-track progress and live rubric movement behind a calm default.

screens.layout: Top: one takeaway sentence in Fraunces, for example 'You opened with discovery and lost the pricing thread at line 8'. Beside it: grade ring, growth delta against the last attempt, and pre-call versus post-call confidence. Then Strengths and one Next rep focus card (one skill, not five). Rubric accordion: each criterion shows bar, rationale and evidence quote chips; tapping a quote replays that transcript line. Full transcript is collapsed at the bottom.

screens.change_vs_today: A long scroll of five equal cards becomes a one-screen takeaway, with evidence one tap away and a single next step.

Main: score trend area chart with a confidence overlay line; a heatmap of criteria by week in sage-to-terracotta tints. Right column: Your next rep card and the past calls list with persona portrait and temperature chip. Filter by job or persona.

screens.layout: 390px width with 16px gutters. Top: compact presence ring (72px) with persona name and state, timer, and an overflow menu holding End call with confirm. Middle: transcript scrolls under the ring. A coach cue peeks as a sheet above the composer; swipe up for the full cue and why. Talk track shows as six dots. Bottom: large Hold to talk button in voice mode, or text field with send in text mode. Touch targets are 48px; the bottom tab bar hides during the call.

screens.change_vs_today: Today the mobile call has a full-width red End button and a chat composer; the coach and hang-up move out of the thumb's way.

live_coaching_and_scoring: The coach is a side channel. The persona session stays in character and never coaches. After each finalized rep turn, a structured-output call (GPT-4.1 mini class, zod schema) returns at most one cue, a talk-track step update and per-criterion deltas, each citing a transcript line. Target: cue within 2 seconds of the rep finishing a turn. Cues are rate-limited (one per 20 seconds; Quiet mode allows three per call). Live scores show as trend arrows, and numbers appear only on toggle. The debrief re-grades the full transcript with the existing weighted rubric, so live and final scores share one rubric and one set of evidence.
persona_library_and_wizard: The library ships about 150 seeded personas as JSON files in /personas, validated by one zod schema. They cover 20 jobs, from SDR cold calls to medical device procurement, and each carries rubric weights and a talk track. Four facets filter them: job, industry, temperature and objection type. The wizard accepts five sources (job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP text, pasted call) and returns a persona, scenario and rubric with source lines. The user edits, runs a dry run, then saves locally or exports a PR-ready file. Community personas get their own tab with credit lines.
signature_moments: Presence ring that breathes with the persona's voice level, replacing the blurry orb
One whispered cue at a time, with a Why tap and a Quiet mode
Quote-to-moment: tap evidence in the debrief and the transcript replays that exact line
Pause and breathe is free and never counts against the score
Wizard exports a persona as a pull request, so a rep's idea can become a merged contribution
openai_fund_angle: Showcase, not footnote. Each call screen carries a model chip (voice model, grader, coach) with a per-call cost estimate. A Model lab in settings swaps models and accepts any OpenAI-compatible base URL, and adds OpenAI Realtime API as a voice provider beside today's ElevenLabs Agents path. The wizard is the flagship GPT demo: structured outputs from a job description or URL. For contributors: 'good first persona' issues, a /personas JSON schema plus AGENTS.md so Codex can add personas, Codex-run PR review on persona files (realism, weights summing to 100), and release-note automation. The landing page shows Realtime, GPT-4.1 mini and Codex badges with a live community persona counter.

implementation.migration_path: Rough phases. Phase 1: Tailwind tokens, shadcn init, icon rail and bottom bar, Fraunces and Inter, replace the orb. Phase 2: move scenarios into /personas JSON with a zod schema, build the library and facet filters. Phase 3: side-channel coach and live read on the call screen. Phase 4: wizard, debrief and progress. Phase 5: manager view, Dusk mode, reduced-motion and mobile QA. Keep the existing grading API contract so debriefs stay backward compatible.

risks: Calm can read as soft. Public reviews of AI sales roleplay tools call the buyer too agreeable or robotic (r/sales thread on Hyperbound and Second Nature). Mitigate with a Hot tier that pushes back and interrupts.
Cue overload and latency. A per-turn coach call adds cost and can distract. Rate limits and Quiet mode are required, and latency must be measured against the 2-second target.

Library claims are unverified. A third-party vendor blog (untitledui.com) says shadcn's default primitive moved to Base UI in July 2026 and that Radix is no longer maintained. Verify on shadcn docs before committing.
The Tailwind 3 to 4 migration touches every screen. Budget for it or stay on v3 and accept more manual work.
Content cost. About 150 personas need human review; AI-drafted personas risk generic objections.
Crowded category. Second Nature, Hyperbound and Yoodli are funded. The open-source version must win on self-hosting, transparency and contributor ownership, not on look alone.
